evidenceToFocusOn: IP geolocation vs. your known locations

UA06.title: Fraud – Chip and PIN Transaction
UA06.description: Chip-and-PIN card used on signature-only POS.

UA10.title: Request Transaction Receipt
UA10.description: Issuer requests receipt for suspected fraud.

UA11.title: Cardholder Claims Fraud (No Signature)
UA11.description: Swipe transaction without signature disputed as fraud.
preventionSteps: Obtain signature or imprint on every transaction.

NA.title: No Authorization
commonMerchantRebuttals: Authorization delayed due to gateway issues
strategyTips: Compare timestamp of charge vs. auth
Show no authorization ever received
Highlight that fallback wasn’t disclosed
NA.customerStrategy: Argue that no proper authorization occurred before the charge, which should invalidate it per network rules.

DA.title: Declined Authorization
preventionSteps: Terminate on decline or request alternate payment.
commonMerchantRebuttals: Customer approved at time of transaction
strategyTips: Highlight repeated decline attempts
Show no later valid auth occurred
Demonstrate lack of fallback logic
DA.customerStrategy: Prove the charge occurred after your card was declined, without your approval or retry.

AT.title: Authorization Noncompliance
AT.description: Processed with expired or no positive auth.

LP.title: Late Presentation
evidenceRequirements: POS receipt date vs. statement post date
commonMerchantRebuttals: System delay caused late batch submission
strategyTips: Compare transaction date and post date
Show expired authorization window
Point out confusion caused by late posting
evidenceToFocusOn: POS receipt date vs. statement post date
LP.customerStrategy: Prove the charge was processed too late to be valid or recognizable, and settlement window expired.

AA.title: Does Not Recognize
strategyTips: Request descriptor breakdown from bank
Show merchant name mismatch
Compare descriptor with past transactions
AA.customerStrategy: Explain that the charge appeared under an unfamiliar name or code, and you had no knowledge or context of the transaction.

AW.title: Altered Amount
strategyTips: Compare initial auth with final posted amount
Confirm no secondary approval occurred
Reference receipt with original pricing
AW.customerStrategy: Show that the amount was altered from what you approved, and no updated consent was captured before processing.

CD.title: Credit/Debit Posted Incorrectly
evidenceRequirements: Bank statement with charge not credit
strategyTips: Prove you were due a credit but a debit was applied
Use merchant confirmation as supporting evidence
Highlight reversal mismatch
evidenceToFocusOn: Bank statement with charge not credit
CD.customerStrategy: Show that a refund was expected but instead a debit was applied in error, causing double billing or negative balance.

DP.title: Duplicate Processing
evidenceRequirements: Proof only one item was delivered
strategyTips: Compare timestamps and descriptions
Highlight identical amounts for same service
Show only one item or service was received
evidenceToFocusOn: Proof only one item was delivered
DP.customerStrategy: Prove that two identical charges were made for the same transaction, and that you only received the service once.
labeledExamples: I was charged twice for the same order.
This is a duplicate posting for one purchase.
The merchant ran the same charge more than once.

PM.title: Paid by Other Means
preventionSteps: Void original sale on alternate payment.

RG.title: Non-Receipt of Goods/Services/Cash
RG.description: Paid but no delivery or pick-up occurred.
strategyTips: Highlight that delivery or service was never completed
Document delivery delays or misrouting
Provide timestamps showing non-fulfillment
RG.customerStrategy: Prove you paid for something that was never delivered, by showing tracking or fulfillment breakdown.
labeledExamples: I paid but never received the goods or service.
I canceled the subscription and was still charged.
The merchant failed to deliver what I purchased.

RM.title: Cardholder Disputes Quality
evidenceRequirements: Visual proof of defect or service issue
strategyTips: Provide photos or transcripts proving poor quality
Compare actual result to promised outcome
Highlight attempts to resolve issue
evidenceToFocusOn: Visual proof of defect or service issue
RM.customerStrategy: Show the goods/services were not as advertised or poorly executed. Use visual proof and your resolution attempts.
labeledExamples: The item was not what the seller described.
What arrived was damaged, defective, or materially different.
The seller misrepresented the purchase.

RN2.title: Credit Not Processed
strategyTips: Show tracking confirming return received
Highlight merchant acknowledgment of return
Prove credit not issued despite confirmation
RN2.customerStrategy: Show the item was returned per policy and the merchant failed to process the refund as promised.
